title: Dedicated Boundary Chronicle: Audit-ready tenant isolation export and sealed manifests
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a hardened evidence export pipeline for dedicated capacity that produces tamper-evident, time-stamped tenant isolation chronicles usable for compliance audits. The feature will collect per-tenant placement, network boundary metadata, disk and VM identifiers, retention policy assertions, and observability traces, then emit a signed, compact manifest bundle that operators and auditors can ingest. The goal is to provide a reproducible chain-of-custody for each audit window and an automated delivery mechanism (S3/GCS/secure-transfer) that integrates with customer retention controls and KMS-backed signing keys.
acceptance_criteria: Collector produces per-tenant boundary records for all dedicated nodes within a configurable window (default 24h)
Manifest bundles include canonicalized JSONL metadata, SHA-256 digests, and an RFC3161-compatible timestamp token
Bundles are signed with a customer-scoped signing key stored in KMS/HSM and verifiable by an external PKI utility
Retention flags and purge markers are embedded and honored by the retention enforcer during export and in on-disk snapshots
Export API supports: dry-run validation, paginated retrieval for multi-window requests, and atomic upload to a configured secure bucket with ACLs
Operator console shows per-export provenance (who triggered, size, included tenants, signature id) and export success/failure metrics
E2E test harness validates end-to-end signature verification and replay of an export into the audit viewer
technical_notes: Collector will subscribe to placement/allocator events and enrich with node telemetry (NIC macs, cloud instance-id, region, AZ)
We will canonicalize records into JSONL using stable key ordering and UTF-8 normalization to avoid signature churn
Manifests will include a Merkle root over payloads to allow partial verification without needing the entire bundle
Time-stamping will call an RFC3161 stamping service (internal or external) and embed the token in the bundle to prove when snapshot was taken
Signing: primary option is KMS asymmetric signing per-customer; fallback is Redwood signing with a notarization chain (use only when customer key not available)
Retention enforcement: export pipeline will run retention checks before exporting; items marked for purge will be excluded and logged with rationale
Transport: first-class support for S3/GCS endpoints + SCP over bastion for air-gapped customers, with retry/backoff and idempotency tokens
Privacy: redact ephemeral IPs from exported docs unless customer explicitly enables full-network export (opt-in), recorded in manifest metadata
Observability: instrument export duration, bytes, objects, signature verification latency, and failed/verifiable counts to runtime-exports dashboard
tasks: Design manifest schema and canonicalization rules (include examples)
Implement collector plugin for dedicated allocator (subscription + enrichment)
Implement bundler service that builds JSONL payloads, computes Merkle root, attaches RFC3161 token, and signs bundle
Build export API with dry-run and pagination endpoints
Integrate KMS signing and fallback signing path; add key rotation and signature metadata
Add retention-enforcer checks and purge-exclusion logging
Add console view for export provenance and link to audit artifacts
Write E2E tests including signature verification and replay into audit viewer
Security review and threat modeling, then run red-team scenario for tamper attempts
Rollout: staged feature flags, canary export runs, and runbook for support teams
